Psalm 38: body imagery may be literal, figurative, or symbolic; no medical diagnosis is inferred.
Psalm 45: Wendland’s proposal of public royal declamation is not independent evidence of a specific performance event.
Psalm 52: Botha’s late Persian-period setting and wisdom-network reconstruction are attributed proposals; the article does not establish a precise composition date or direct literary dependence.

Psalm 59: Janowski’s evening-to-morning reading is a literary interpretation. The relation of the repeated prayer/refrain and any historical occasion remain unresolved; the superscription is not used to date composition.

Psalms 61 and 63: LeMon’s publisher abstract alone was accessible. Entries report only the abstract’s proposal that the bulla analysis strengthens a royal-voice reading; no bulla details, provenance, independent archaeological conclusion, or full-article argument is claimed.
Psalm 64: Eder’s narratological sequence describes the poem’s literary movement; it does not establish a prose historical event, performance setting, or composition date.
Psalm 65: Botha’s proposed Psalms 65–68 editorial cluster and Zion-to-earth sequence are interpretations, not proof of a specific cultic rite, historical event, or date.

Psalm 98: Blunda Grubert’s full article was inaccessible; only the Spanish publisher abstract supports the limited group-level framing.

Psalm 141: only Booij’s publisher abstract was accessible; the proposed pronoun and lexical readings are low-confidence, and the article’s national-distress setting is not adopted.

All eight A11 records remain draft/in-review with human review required; no human reviewer is named.

Psalm 40: Jassen’s 2006 publisher abstract was accessible, but not the full article; the 4Q160 reuse proposal remains abstract-limited and does not identify 4Q160 as a biblical manuscript witness.
Psalm 73: Wong’s 2016 publisher abstract was accessible, but not the full article; the ring-composition proposal remains low-confidence pending inspection of its structural argument.
Psalm 78: Kim and van Rooy’s full 2000 article was inspected, but proposed structure, genre, date, and Sitz im Leben remain disputed; no date or performance setting is asserted.
